chose: the shared EVOLUTION store (src/evolution.ts) is an IN-PROCESS MEMO keyed <root>|<limit>, and persists nothing
over: a status.json evolution/churn section written by every history-reading command
a committed churn artifact under outputDir keyed by HEAD
leaving the derivation spelled three times (decompose, drift, scene) and only documenting the duplication
because: the finding was REDUNDANCY, not latency: one git derivation spelled three times, with the BULK band and a bare 200-commit window free to drift apart. A persisted cache fixes the wrong problem and adds a new one — it would be rewritten by every command that touches history and land in every diff a reader has to review, so the repo pays perpetual diff noise for a git call the CLI makes a handful of times per process. The memo is valid because the CLI is one command per process and HEAD cannot move underneath it; _resetEvolutionMemo() exists so a test process, the one place that assumption is false, can drop it.

chose: the command is named `mass` and there is no umbrella verb over it
over: `energy` — an assembler command that would run mass + drift + churn and print one composite score
folding the mass dimensions into `decompose` or `drift` as extra sections
because: MASS is the thing actually measured: lines, files, symbols, dependency counts, and whatever the project's own measures probe. It is a scalar the ratchet can pin, and every dimension is addressable by key — which is what makes a baseline, a tolerance and a --raise subject possible. `energy` would name a composite nobody can point at: a score assembled from a snapshot plus a derivative has no unit, no baseline that means anything, and no key to hang a tolerance on. An umbrella command would also make the failure ambiguous — a reader could not tell which instrument said no.

chose: a mass excursion becomes a journal entry ONLY under --raise, as a Finding fed through raiseFindings
over: calling `observed` implicitly for every dimension on every run, so mass fed the tracked-metric machinery automatically
writing a conjecture directly from mass.ts, bypassing the cap and the dedupe
because: `observed` is for a metric whose owner has already declared a BAND — value, baseline, threshold — so 'outside' means something the harness did not invent. Mass has no band: the baseline is a PIN, and a pin plus a tolerance of zero would make every ordinary growth run an implicit journal write on a read-only report. That is precisely the surprising-write failure raise.ts's header says kills a mechanism wholesale. Going through raiseFindings also buys the two things a hand-rolled write loses: the per-run cap spent round-robin across advisories, and dedupe on a subject that carries no magnitude — so a second run after another 400 lines does not mint a second question about lines|total.

chose: the mass ratchet's growth failure PRESCRIBES `coherence decide` — it says the movement gained parts nobody named, then names the two commands that settle it
over: printing a silent numeric diff (lines|total 4 → 9) and letting the reader decide what to do
failing with a generic 'threshold exceeded' and a link to the config key
because: a numeric diff tells the reader what `git diff --stat` already told them and settles nothing. The ratchet cannot know whether 460 new lines bought a feature or an accident, and the only party who can say is the one who wrote them — this run, while they still remember, not a reader six months out. So the gate does not ask for justification, it asks for a RECORD and then a re-pin: `coherence decide "<what the new mass buys>"` followed by `--update-baseline`. That also makes the re-pin honest — the baseline moves with an entry beside it saying why, instead of moving because somebody wanted the build green.

chose: a per-component mass key falls back to the DIR (`lines|.`) when no component node carries a label, never to the raw graph id (`lines|c:.`)
over: decompose's componentMap fallback (`compLabel.get(parent) ?? parent`), which yields the raw `c:<dir>` id
because: the first dogfood run of `coherence mass` on this repo — which declares no components — printed `lines|c:.`, and that key would then have been written into mass-baseline.json, quoted in --check failures and used as a --raise subject for the life of the project. A baseline key is an ADDRESS somebody types; a graph-internal id escaping into it is the kind of leak that is impossible to rename later because it is in everyone's committed baseline. decompose's fallback is fine where it lives (an in-memory grouping label nobody stores).

chose: the harness's own last 400 commits show a NET +22,898 LOC, but `mass` measures the tree at 19,898 lines — the history added more than the repo currently holds, over a window that does not obviously reach the repo's first commit
couldBe: the two instruments count different FILE SETS: git counts every tracked file (README.md at 111KB, RELEASE-NOTES.md, the .coherence journal, public/ artifacts when they were tracked), while mass counts only the 76 nodes in the derived graph (src + test .ts)
the window is not the whole history: 400 commits may reach back past a large deletion, so net-over-window and current-size are simply not comparable quantities
churn: rewrites delete and re-add the same region, and --shortstat counts both sides, so net can exceed final size wherever a file was rewritten rather than appended to
discriminatedBy: run `git log --shortstat` over the SAME 400 commits restricted to the graph's own paths (`-- src test`) and compare the net to lines|total; then repeat with no -n limit. If the path-restricted net lands near 19,898 the file-set explanation wins; if only the unlimited range does, the window explanation wins; if neither closes the gap, it is churn and the two numbers were never comparable.

chose: the two instruments count different FILE SETS
because: Ran the discriminating test. (1) The WINDOW candidate is dead outright: `git rev-list --count HEAD` is 80, so the 400-commit window already spans the entire history — net(400) and net(all) are the same number, 22,898. (2) Scoping the same all-history --shortstat to the graph's own paths (`-- src test`) gives net +18,995 against a measured lines|total of 19,898, and the residual is accounted for by the four files this change added being present in the graph and absent from any commit. The 3,903-line gap is README.md (111KB), RELEASE-NOTES.md and the .coherence journal — tracked by git, invisible to the graph walk. (3) Churn is therefore at most a minor term, not the explanation. Consequence: the report now NAMES the universe on the spark line ('ALL tracked files, not just the graph's'), because printing two numbers from two different file sets in one report is how a reader ends up distrusting the wrong instrument.
